017package org.apache.juneau.rest.client.mcp.auth;
018
019import static org.apache.juneau.commons.utils.AssertionUtils.*;
020
021import java.net.*;
022import java.util.*;
023
024/**
025 * Builds the pair of loopback redirect URIs (SEP-837 loopback redirect handling) an MCP native/CLI client registers
026 * with an authorization server during Dynamic Client Registration.
027 *
028 * <p>
029 * The MCP client-registration spec's CIMD example registers <b>both</b> {@code http://127.0.0.1} and
030 * {@code http://localhost} forms of the callback so the authorization server accepts whichever the operating system's
031 * browser resolves the loopback interface to.  Two strategies are supported (RFC 8252 &sect;7.3), both fully usable
032 * end-to-end (the acquirer binds the port that was registered):
033 * <ul>
034 *    <li><b>Port-agnostic</b> ({@link #portAgnostic(String)}) &mdash; the <b>easy default</b>: register the two host-only
035 *       forms and rely on RFC 8252 &sect;7.3 loopback port-agnostic matching (a spec-conformant authorization server MUST
036 *       permit any port on a loopback redirect).  The acquirer then binds an ephemeral port and no coordination is needed.
037 *    <li><b>Bind-first</b> ({@link #forPort(int, String)}) &mdash; for <b>strict exact-match</b> authorization servers
038 *       that reject port-agnostic loopback redirects: register the two port-bearing forms for a caller-chosen fixed port,
039 *       then bind that same fixed port on the acquirer (via {@link McpAuthorizationCodeAcquirer.Builder#redirectPort(int)},
040 *       wired automatically by {@link McpClientRegistrations#configure}) so the receiver listens on exactly the port the
041 *       authorization server was told.
042 * </ul>
043 *
044 * @since 10.0.0
045 */
046public final class LoopbackRedirectUris {
047
048   private LoopbackRedirectUris() {}
049
050   /**
051    * Returns the port-agnostic loopback redirect URIs (RFC 8252 &sect;7.3): {@code http://127.0.0.1<path>} and
052    * {@code http://localhost<path>}.
053    *
054    * @param path The callback path (must start with {@code /}).  Must not be <jk>null</jk> or blank.
055    * @return An immutable, order-preserving list of the two loopback redirect URIs.  Never <jk>null</jk>.
056    */
057   public static List<URI> portAgnostic(String path) {
058      var p = assertArgNotNullOrBlank("path", path);
059      assertArg(p.startsWith("/"), "path must start with '/' (was '%s')", p);
060      return List.of(
061         URI.create("http://127.0.0.1" + p),
062         URI.create("http://localhost" + p));
063   }
064
065   /**
066    * Returns the port-bearing loopback redirect URIs (bind-first strategy): {@code http://127.0.0.1:<port><path>} and
067    * {@code http://localhost:<port><path>}.
068    *
069    * <p>
070    * Register these for a caller-chosen fixed port, then bind that same port on the acquirer
071    * ({@link McpAuthorizationCodeAcquirer.Builder#redirectPort(int)}) so the receiver listens on exactly the port the
072    * authorization server was told.
073    *
074    * @param port The fixed loopback port to register (and later bind on the receiver).  Must be in {@code 1..65535}.
075    * @param path The callback path (must start with {@code /}).  Must not be <jk>null</jk> or blank.
076    * @return An immutable, order-preserving list of the two loopback redirect URIs.  Never <jk>null</jk>.
077    */
078   public static List<URI> forPort(int port, String path) {
079      assertArg(port >= 1 && port <= 65535, "port must be in 1..65535 (was %s)", port);
080      var p = assertArgNotNullOrBlank("path", path);
081      assertArg(p.startsWith("/"), "path must start with '/' (was '%s')", p);
082      return List.of(
083         URI.create("http://127.0.0.1:" + port + p),
084         URI.create("http://localhost:" + port + p));
085   }
086}
